North York Moors: Scenic Motorcycle Roads

The North York Moors National Park offers a distinctive riding experience — vast purple heather moorlands, dramatic coastal cliffs, deep wooded valleys, and roads that flow across the landscape like ribbons on a map. It's one of England's best-kept biking secrets.

The A170 Escarpment

The A170 from Thirsk to Scarborough climbs Sutton Bank — one of England's most dramatic road climbs. The gradient is severe (1 in 4) and the views from the top across the Vale of York are legendary. From here, the road crosses the moors via Helmsley to the coast.

Moorland Roads

  • Blakey Ridge: The road from Hutton-le-Hole to Castleton crosses the highest ground in the Moors. In August, the heather turns the landscape purple as far as you can see. The Lion Inn at Blakey Ridge is one of England's most isolated pubs.
  • Rosedale Chimney: A fierce 1-in-3 climb out of Rosedale with hairpin bends and views across the valley. Challenging but exhilarating.
  • Wheeldale Moor: Open moorland roads with views to the coast. Roman road remains nearby add historical interest.

The Coast

  • Whitby to Robin Hood's Bay: The coastal road between these fishing villages offers dramatic clifftop views and drops down into Robin Hood's Bay — a village that tumbles down to the sea.
  • Staithes: A hidden fishing village in a narrow ravine. The ride down to the harbour is steep and atmospheric.
  • Ravenscar: The "town that never was" — a Victorian development that failed, leaving dramatic clifftop views and a sense of isolation.
The North York Moors are most beautiful in August when heather blooms turn the moorland purple. The contrast of purple heather, green valleys, and the blue North Sea on the horizon is uniquely English.

Day Ride Suggestion (120 miles)

  • Start Helmsley → Sutton Bank viewpoint → Rievaulx Abbey → Blakey Ridge → Wheeldale Moor → Whitby → Robin Hood's Bay → Scarborough → return via A170
  • This route covers moorland, valley, and coast in a single satisfying day

Food and Drink Stops

The North York Moors has excellent food stops for touring riders. The Star Inn at Harome holds a Michelin star and is worth a special stop for a memorable lunch. For more casual eating, the fish and chips in Whitby are legendarily good — the Magpie Cafe has been serving them since 1939.

The Lion Inn at Blakey Ridge, one of England's most isolated pubs at the heart of the moorland, serves hearty food and local ales. It's been serving travellers since 1553 and the atmosphere is unchanged by centuries. In winter, the fire is roaring; in summer, the terrace views across the purple moors are magnificent.

Helmsley, the gateway to the western moors, is a handsome market town with a castle, independent shops, and excellent cafes. It makes an ideal start or finish point for a moors ride, with good motorcycle parking in the main square.
keyTakeaways: The A170 climbs Sutton Bank, one of England's most dramatic road climbs at 1 in 4, with legendary views across the Vale of York.
Blakey Ridge crosses the highest ground in the Moors, turning purple with heather in August, home to the isolated Lion Inn.
Rosedale Chimney is a fierce 1-in-3 climb with hairpins, challenging but exhilarating.
The suggested 120-mile day ride links moorland, valley and coast from Helmsley to Whitby and back.
August is the peak season when blooming heather sets purple moor against green valleys and the blue North Sea.

faq.q: When are the moors at their most spectacular?
faq.a: August is the standout month, when the heather blooms and turns the moorland purple as far as you can see. The contrast of purple heather, green valleys and the blue North Sea on the horizon is uniquely English. Blakey Ridge and Wheeldale Moor are among the best places to experience it. Outside August the moors are still atmospheric, but lack that signature colour.

faq.q: How steep is the Rosedale Chimney climb?
faq.a: Rosedale Chimney is a fierce climb of around 1 in 3 out of Rosedale, with hairpin bends and views across the valley. It is challenging but exhilarating, and demands confidence with steep hill starts and tight turns. Sutton Bank on the A170 is another severe climb at 1 in 4. Both are best tackled in dry conditions with a clear run at the gradient.

faq.q: What is a good day ride in the Moors?
faq.a: A satisfying 120-mile circuit starts at Helmsley, climbs to the Sutton Bank viewpoint, visits Rievaulx Abbey, crosses Blakey Ridge and Wheeldale Moor, then drops to Whitby and Robin Hood's Bay before running down to Scarborough and returning via the A170. This route packs moorland, valley and coast into a single satisfying day, with the Lion Inn a natural mid-ride stop.

faq.q: Where should I stop for food?
faq.a: Whitby's fish and chips are legendary, and the Magpie Cafe has been serving them since 1939. The Lion Inn at Blakey Ridge, one of England's most isolated pubs at the heart of the moorland, has served travellers since 1553 and offers hearty food, local ales and terrace views across the purple moors. Helmsley is a handsome market town with good cafes and easy motorcycle parking.
